bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission relating to "Commission Guidance Regarding the Listing of Voluntary Carbon Credit Derivative Contracts".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the final guidance issued by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) titled Commission Guidance Regarding the Listing of Voluntary Carbon Credit Derivative Contracts and published on October 15, 2024. The guidance provides factors for designated contract markets (i.e., CFTC-regulated derivatives exchanges) to consider when listing voluntary carbon credit derivative contracts, including characteristics of transparency and permanence.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn guidance issued by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in October 2024 concerning how exchanges should list derivatives contracts tied to voluntary carbon credits. The guidance had outlined factors such as transparency and permanence that exchanges should consider when offering these carbon-credit-based financial products. If passed, the resolution would nullify that guidance and leave exchanges without the CFTC's framework for listing such contracts.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects derivatives exchanges and financial institutions that trade or list carbon credit derivative contracts.
Fossil fuel companies participate in carbon credit markets and may use derivative contracts to manage carbon-related financial exposure.
Renewable energy projects often generate carbon credits that underlie these derivative contracts, affecting their market access and pricing mechanisms.
Agricultural operations generate carbon credits through practices like carbon sequestration, making them participants in the voluntary carbon credit market.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the final guidance issued by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission titled Commission Guidance Regarding the Listing of Voluntary Carbon Credit Derivative Contracts and published on October 15, 2024.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in dealing with banks and lenders. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
